title: Securities Trading Policy
date_approved: 22 June 2022 (Board approval of update; originally approved 31 March 2016)

tiers.name: Relevant Persons
tiers.description: All officers of the Group, all employees, all contractors and agents to the extent they possess price sensitive information about the Group known to them only by virtue of their engagement, and in certain circumstances their associates. Substantive prohibitions (Closed Periods, short-term dealing, notification, hedging of unvested plan securities) apply to this collective tier.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: A director of the Group; distinguished for clearance only: must inform and receive approval from the Chairman before undertaking a transaction.

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: The Chairman of the Board; distinguished for clearance only: must inform and obtain approval from the Board or the next most senior independent director before undertaking a transaction.

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: Employees of the Group; distinguished for clearance only: must inform and receive approval from the Managing Director or Company Secretary before undertaking a transaction.

tiers.name: Other Relevant Persons
tiers.description: Relevant Persons other than directors, the Chairman and employees (e.g. contractors and agents); must inform and receive approval from the Company Secretary or, in his absence, the Managing Director.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Directors, officers and other Key Management Personnel (as defined in Australian Accounting Standard 124) of the Group; subject to an express prohibition on using their securities holding as collateral for margin lending, subject to grandfathering of facilities existing before 1 March 2016.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Associates as defined in the Corporations Act, including immediate family or any entity for which the Relevant Person controls investment decisions; the Relevant Person must notify the Company Secretary of dealing by associates of which the Relevant Person has knowledge.

definitions.hedging_definition: a transaction if the transaction effectively operates to hedge or limit the economic risk of securities allocated under the Group's employee incentive plans during the period those securities remain unvested or subject to restrictions under the terms of the plan

windows.end_anchor: 12 noon (AEST) on the next business day after the day on which the Group's full-year results are released
12 noon (AEST) on the next business day after the day on which the Group's half-year results are released

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The policy permits the 'Company' to notify Relevant Persons that they may not buy and sell securities outside a Closed Period; the deciding officer and confidentiality of such a notification are not specified.

rules.detail: No express OTC derivatives rule. Securities extends to 'things relating to securities issued by the Group (eg., warrants and other derivative products)' and Dealing extends to exercising options and entering agreements to buy or sell securities, so an OTC put/call is caught as a Dealing requiring clearance under 2)b)ii) and is barred in Closed Periods and while holding inside information.
rules.evidence: Dealing in securities is a broad concept and covers more than simply buying or selling securities. It extends to exercising options over securities and entering agreements to buy or sell securities.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on transactions that effectively hedge or limit the economic risk of securities allocated under employee incentive plans while unvested.
rules.evidence: must not enter into a transaction if the transaction effectively operates to hedge or limit the economic risk of securities allocated under the Group's employee incentive plans during the period those securities remain unvested or subject to restrictions under the terms of the plan.

rules.detail: The same express hedging ban extends to plan securities that have vested but remain subject to restrictions under the plan's terms.
rules.evidence: must not enter into a transaction if the transaction effectively operates to hedge or limit the economic risk of securities allocated under the Group's employee incentive plans during the period those securities remain unvested or subject to restrictions under the terms of the plan.

rules.detail: Once restrictions cease, dealings in plan securities (the policy gives hedging-style dealing as its own example: 'eg., following cessation of restrictions over the securities') must only occur in accordance with the general policy, i.e. ordinary clearance, Closed Period and insider trading rules; hedging is not separately named at this stage.
rules.evidence: While Relevant Persons remain employed by the Group, any dealings in the Group's securities (eg., following cessation of restrictions over the securities) acquired under security plans operated by the Group must only occur in accordance with this policy.

rules.detail: Monetisation itself is not named, but forward contracts are given as the example of a short-term dealing requiring clearance; a prepaid forward or similar monetisation structure falls within this express carve-in.
rules.evidence: In addition, Relevant Persons may not enter into any other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts) except with clearance under clause b)ii).

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.

CFDs are not named. A CFD is a financial product referencing the Group's securities and would fall within the broad 'entering agreements to buy or sell securities' concept of Dealing, and in practice within the ban on short-term or speculative dealing, requiring clearance.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons may not deal in any of the Group's securities on a short term or speculative trading basis, except in circumstances of special hardship and with clearance under clause b)ii).

rules.detail: Directors, officers and other KMP are banned from using their Group securities holding as collateral for margin lending. Facilities in existence before 1 March 2016 are grandfathered subject to notifying the Chairman of margin calls, material breach or a 90%+ loan-to-value ratio, and undertaking to cure within one month.
rules.evidence: directors, officers and other “Key Management Personnel” (as defined in Australian Accounting Standard 124) of the Group are prohibited from using his or her holding in any of the Group's securities as collateral for any margin lending.

rules.detail: The express margin lending prohibition is limited to directors, officers and other KMP; it is not extended to other employees, contractors, agents or associates.

Granting security over Group securities to a margin lender is prohibited for KMP as part of the margin lending ban; a charge or lien unconnected to margin lending, or granted by non-KMP, is not addressed.
rules.evidence: prohibited from using his or her holding in any of the Group's securities as collateral for any margin lending.

rules.detail: The prohibition is expressly framed as 'margin lending' collateral only, not 'any secured financing arrangement'; whether a bank collar loan secured on shares with margin-call/LVR features falls within 'margin lending' is not defined in the policy.
rules.evidence: directors, officers and other “Key Management Personnel” ... of the Group are prohibited from using his or her holding in any of the Group's securities as collateral for any margin lending.

rules.detail: No general prohibition on secured financing or encumbrance applies outside the KMP margin lending clause.
Buying and selling within a 3 month period is banned except in circumstances of special hardship and with clearance.
rules.evidence: That is, Relevant Persons may not buy and sell securities within a 3 month period.

financing.price_trigger_guidance: reaches 90% or above of any applicable loan-to-value ratio or other asset cover
financing_disclosure: Key Management Personnel with grandfathered pre-1 March 2016 margin loans: trigger = margin call or similar (reasonably expected), material breach entitling the lender to sell, or reaching 90%+ loan-to-value ratio/asset cover; to the Chairman of the Board, in writing; deadline within five business days of becoming aware.

exemption_authority: The relevant clearance officer under clause 2)b)ii) (Chairman for directors; Board or senior independent director for the Chairman; Managing Director or Company Secretary for employees; Company Secretary or Managing Director for other Relevant Persons) may grant prior clearance to deal during a Closed Period or on a short-term basis in cases of severe financial hardship or other exceptional circumstances such as a court order, enforceable undertaking or bona fide family settlement; confidentiality of any refusal is not addressed.

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin lending ban is KMP-only and margin-loan-specific
bespoke_clauses.clause: directors, officers and other “Key Management Personnel” ... of the Group are prohibited from using his or her holding in any of the Group's securities as collateral for any margin lending.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The express prohibition is confined to KMP and to 'margin lending'; other employees and contractors face no express bar on pledging shares, and even for KMP whether a bank's collar-secured loan counts as 'margin lending' (rather than another form of secured financing) is undefined and would need to be tested.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Key Management Person with security over his or her holding ... in connection with margin lending which is in existence prior to 1 March 2016 will not be in breach ... provided that the Key Management Person notifies the Chairman ... within five business days of becoming aware that his or her margin loan facility ... is subject to a margin call, in material breach, or reaches 90% or above of any applicable loan-to-value ratio.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any new collar-secured loan post-dates 1 March 2016 and so cannot rely on this grandfathering; it confirms the general rule is a forward-looking ban on new KMP margin/secured lending against Group shares.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban tied to vesting/restriction status only
bespoke_clauses.clause: must not enter into a transaction if the transaction effectively operates to hedge or limit the economic risk of securities allocated under the Group's employee incentive plans during the period those securities remain unvested or subject to restrictions under the terms of the plan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Once plan securities vest and restrictions lapse, hedging is no longer expressly banned and only ordinary Dealing clearance and Closed Period rules apply, so the collar's put/call legs over vested unrestricted shares are structurally available subject to clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Dealing in securities is a broad concept and covers more than simply buying or selling securities. It extends to exercising options over securities and entering agreements to buy or sell securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Granting a charge or lien is not listed as a form of Dealing, so outside the KMP margin lending clause, pledging shares to secure a loan is not independently regulated by this policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Relevant Person must notify the Company Secretary: before, or immediately after, any buying or selling by them ... of Group securities at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entry into, unwind of, or settlement under a collar (to the extent treated as buying or selling) must be notified to the Company Secretary regardless of Closed Period status, creating an ongoing disclosure trail for the bank's structure.

summary: A funded collar is workable in part but faces a real gap on the financing leg. The put and call over vested, unrestricted shares would be a Dealing requiring prior clearance (Chairman for directors; Managing Director or Company Secretary for employees; Company Secretary or Managing Director for other Relevant Persons), executed outside the two annual Closed Periods and not while short-term (within 3 months of acquisition) or while holding inside information, with notification to the Company Secretary before or immediately after dealing. Hedging is only expressly banned while the plan securities remain unvested or restriction-locked, so hedging vested unrestricted shares is permitted with clearance. However, for directors, officers and other Key Management Personnel, using their Group securities as collateral for margin lending is expressly prohibited (subject only to a narrow pre-1 March 2016 grandfather), and it is unclear whether a bank collar loan secured on shares with margin-call features would be characterised as 'margin lending' and caught by this ban; for other employees and contractors there is no equivalent express prohibition. Structuring the loan leg to avoid the 'margin lending' label, or restricting the funded collar to non-KMP employees, would materially improve feasibility, but KMP participation carries real prohibition risk absent a policy carve-out.
